observation: Plan-authoring missed behavioral coupling between pointer-hover and state in slash-menu despite the component's onMouseEnter binding being documented. Critique r0 caught the unsatisfiable validation scenario (hover A + select B impossible if hover sets selected); designer re-targeted to TabBar as reference. Root cause: the plan author did not trace the pointer-event chain to setSelectedIndex before writing the className-only fix — behavior and chrome authoring siloed.

Critique r1 surfaced new AC validation mismatch: TabBar focus e2e assertion copied row bg-mix behavior but TabBar implements two-tone via text-color + border, not bg. Assertion would fail on correct TabBar (background assertion against transparent bg). Critique caught at r1 review, not red-phase authoring.

Builder reported 'verify passed' for e2e specs but specs were unreachable: red tests authored against lazy-rendered catalog component (DesignSystem defaults to modules[0]) and never navigated to TabBar/Button/Input sections. Specs were written in red phase against a catalog structure assumption without validating the DOM would be present. Root cause: no primitive-host pattern yet (CC-018). Plan assumed catalog navigation would work; red tests never validated the navigation path existed.

Code review (Phase 4) found 8/11 AI6 e2e tests failing due to DOM-selector unreachability + missing navigation. Builder's 'verify passed' signal was a false green — e2e never actually ran. This is a real cost: builder confidence in the verify signal was broken. The builder fixed it in Phase 4 (not Phase 3); code review caught what verify should have caught.

TabBar pill focus (outline-1) was in the plan explicitly (architecture.md:57) but was missed on first green pass (line 73 remained outline-[2px]). TabBar is the AC's reference implementation and now carries two divergent focus treatments (1px underline, 2px pill). No lint rule exists for outline-width, so the divergence passed silent. Fixed in Phase 4 review, not Phase 3 red.

Architecture critique r0 was stream-of-consciousness on tracking-AC verification (cell says 'is wrong', then 'also wrong', then 'correct'), making the AC section unreviewable and contradicting itself mid-text. Critique r1 required a rewrite to state only the chosen method. Pattern: verifiability (Dimension 9) can fail even when the final answer is correct if the reasoning is presented as a thought-process rather than a clean decision.

Reality reconciliation (CC-007) was exemplary: plan made nearly every file:line claim about existing code and all were verified against source. `no-raw-tailwind-color.ts:43`, `util.ts:277`, `collectClassStringsFromJSXAttribute`, `RAW_TAILWIND_PALETTE` all matched spec exactly. This is the dimension most plans fail; AI6 nailed it via aggressive spec-vs-source diffing.

TDD red-then-green paid off: once e2e specs were fixed to actually navigate the catalog (Phase 4), all 15 passing specs confirm ACs work. The implementation was correct; the proof-of-concept in red phase had the wrong assumptions (catalog structure). Fixing the assumptions + re-running turned red to green.

Dual critique loop (design + architecture, then r1 re-critique) caught 5 separate real issues: slash-menu behavioral coupling, TabBar hover assertion shape, StatusChip ownership ambiguity, ESLint premise stale, and focus assertion scope. Multi-round critique defended against plan-authoring blind spots.

HTML reference tracking migration was authored in the plan but skipped on first green pass (task 10 was not applied — ArtifactEmbed/Preview/Block.html never migrated letter-spacing). Plan explicitly rejected deferral. Builder then skipped it. Gap between plan mandate and green completion; caught in code review, not red/green phases.
